body: Shadow Hearts: From the New World is Nautilus's PlayStation 2 role-playing game, first released in Japan on 28 July 2005. Johnny Garland, an amnesiac private investigator, travels with Shania in pursuit of the dangerous Lady through an alternate Prohibition-era America. The setting combines recognisable places and history with supernatural horror and eccentric companions. A new cast gives the series another starting point while retaining its timing-based battles. The journey becomes an investigation whose strange encounters matter both to the mystery and to the party gradually assembled around it.

The Judgement Ring asks the player to time an input within marked areas after selecting an action. Combat therefore adds a physical performance to the usual decision about which character should attack, heal or use a skill. A party of up to four characters brings different abilities into that system. Choosing an effective plan is only part of carrying it out; the player must still execute the ring input reliably. The repeated timing gives otherwise familiar role-playing battles another rhythm, keeping attention on each action instead of treating its selection as the end of the turn.

Takamusa Ohsawa directed and produced the game after working on Covenant, with Miyako Kato returning to design the characters. Yoshitaka Hirota led a score also credited to Tomoko Imoto and Ryo Fukuda. The North American release followed in 2006 and Europe in 2007. Development focused on refining the preceding game's mechanics while introducing a new setting and group. It became Nautilus's final game before the studio was absorbed into Aruze and left development, closing the original series with another mixture of historical travel, improbable personalities and carefully timed combat.
